scenes.say: Ever wonder if your HTML tags can make your site more accessible and easier to maintain? Let’s talk semantic HTML.

scenes.label: Meaning
scenes.sub: Semantic elements show what content is about.
scenes.say: Semantic elements like header or main tell browsers and developers what each part of your page means.
For example, using article for news content makes it clear this section is a standalone story.

rows.b: Code is easier to read and maintain

scenes.say: Semantic HTML improves accessibility, boosts search rankings, and makes your code much clearer.

scenes.question: Should you use div for main content?
scenes.right: No, use main to show it's the primary content.
scenes.say: Interviewers might ask if you can use div for main content. Actually, main is better because it signals the primary section to browsers and assistive tech.
